I've been farming this same land for 15 years. I know what works here and what doesn't. My wife's brother works in the city so it's mostly me and my wife doing the farm work, with help during busy times. Water is getting harder — the well is deeper than it was ten years ago — so I try not to waste irrigation.

My 13.1 mu splits naturally: 8 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, and 5.1 mu for cotton. Cotton prices have been okay the last couple years and I know how to manage it, so I'm keeping it.

**Wheat:** I'll plant Jimai 22 — it's what most people around here use, the seed station carries it, and I've had good results. I'll do base fertilizer before planting and top-dress at jointing. Three irrigations: winter water in December to protect against freeze, jointing stage, and heading. Rotary till after maize harvest to break up the stubble. I'll spray herbicide in February and do one or two fungicide/aphid treatments in April-May.

**Maize:** Direct seed right after wheat harvest in June — no time to till, and frankly no-till works fine for summer maize. I'll use Zhengdan 958, it's reliable and everyone here uses it. July and August we usually get rain so I only need to irrigate once or twice. One herbicide pass early on, one pest spray mid-season.

**Cotton:** Plough in March, transplant or direct seed in late April. I'll use a Bt hybrid to reduce bollworm pressure. Cotton needs potassium — I'll put more K here than on the grain crops. Four irrigations spread from June through August. Even with Bt I'll spray four times — aphids and mites still show up.
